settings.scope: credible Linux loader prototype with original unrestricted test mods

M3-W0.evidence: docs/architecture/m3-hook-targets.md and the pinned 26.1.2 hook inventory

M3-W2.evidence: command, event, resource, and data conformance suites

M3-W4.evidence: Ravel has moved its own versioned bytes through an official world save, a clean exit, and a reload. `ravel-composed-host` carries `ravel-test-mod-saved-data` from change uyvzkzzstmrsunzxznznwqorvxslnklr, so the production composition owns world data rather than only modelling it; the game's own SavedDataStorage wrote `data/ravel/mods.dat` into a world it created, the reload read the aggregate back byte-identical, and a stored dataVersion rewritten to 9 outside the game was refused with the diagnostic drawn in the client. See evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json under worldPersistenceRoundTrip. The ceiling is recorded in the same place and in risks below: the live half is operator attestation, not a result a reviewer can recompute, because the world and the raw logs were deleted and only digests survive. The in-gate half — tests/conformance/tests/saved_data.rs and jvm/harness/PersistenceMain.java — runs on every gate.

M3-W7.evidence: evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json records result pass at 33 callable targets over 15 classes: the three Ravel screens, the configuration round trip including a restart-required setting, the command path, opt-in profiling, and the Ravel-owned world round trip that M3-W4 turns on. The one surface that failed on first observation — the profiling report's two clipped lines — was fixed by change npozznqztnvnuvuvunkmsuvvvplnvkxq and re-observed whole in a real client. The same ceiling applies as to M3-W4: this is an operator-run result, checkable by a reviewer only for its in-gate half. Two named gaps stay open inside a closed gate and are recorded in openGaps: nothing on the game's tick path marks a tick boundary, so the tick counter cannot leave zero, and the command counter, which is wired and accurate, has never been observed above zero in a real client because no launch yet combined a command-claiming mod with a namespaced command.

M3-W8.evidence: The earliest independent round returned FAIL with four findings, and all four are now answered. That round's verdict text was never written into the repository and is not recoverable from it: what follows is the summary, which evidence/m3/review.md now names as the one round it does not hold. The four findings were the manifest inventory omission of M3-W0; the package-schema contradiction, which change rkrpplvwpklskyuwvksvmuuyklkwsqlt closed by migrating schemas/package.schema.json in place so that targets is refused and source declares a repository plus integrity-protected portable files; the missing Ravel-owned versioned world write, closed under M3-W4; and the unexercised native surfaces, closed under M3-W7. A later review round found four more against the evidence set itself rather than the prototype: the manifest recorded digests nothing recomputed, it pinned a revision predating the work it covered, it contradicted the other records on whether the world round trip had happened, and one record self-declared a pass the manifest held open. Those are answered by change pqkoksqopryuyvzormzsnllylmusvtpp and by the digest check verify_evidence_records added in yuouxpsvvstnoquzxxsrwktmzrlmmlvy. Clean results: hook integrity passed, safety/layering/ADR conformance passed, and redaction passed. Four further rounds followed, so evidence/m3/review.md holds five verbatim verdicts and names the earliest round as the one it does not hold. The fourth of the five found the omitted verdict text described above, two counts in evidence/m3/README.md that no longer described the tree, an unfollowable derivation in evidence/m3/profiling-overhead.json, and two deviation-grade holes recorded below; all of those are answered. The fifth found one blocking defect, B-1: the caveat re-observation campaign in evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json bound the reading that proves the profiling surface renders whole to screen-jar and native-library digests written before change lppyxtnzxzstoxqozxttumntmnpulzxs, the change whose effect that reading reports, so the campaign's stated launch count and artifact set could not both be true and no digest existed for the build the reading came from. B-1 is now answered by observation rather than by rewording. A fifth launch campaign, profilingReObservationCampaign in the same record, built the screen jar and the native library, staged both in a private owner-only directory, hashed them there before the game started, and read the profiling report at both GUI scales on one title-only launch: screen jar 242d855c7e91fb9d68b3d228683ef59726b691bda972653524ae41a833601729, native library b7ac133e1902269dcb4f8781dd23998888d614775a1f99996524c310ac1ded86, agent jar unchanged at 404740f4c466262f8be4495a29490f043ebb1df98ee4e0710995b51b33810981. At scale 1 the whole twelve-line report rendered, naming all six unmeasurable metrics including tick-count, with the summary stating no tick figure; at the default scale the documented seven-row budget kept the summary, heading and accuracy statement and dropped the rest without truncating anything. The unattributable reading is withdrawn where it stood rather than restated at another number, and screens.profiling.provenance now names which campaign each row belongs to. Two of the same round's must-fix findings are fixed in the same pass: the repealed reviewer note in matrixNotCarriedForward.whatThisMeansForAReviewer, and the rewrite count in howItWasResolved, which now distinguishes the two world-opening surface launches at 15 classes and 33 methods from the title-only launch at 11 and 27. Still unanswered: that round's third must-fix finding, its five moderate findings including the absence of any M3-specific manifest closure rule, and its six minor ones. M3-W8 stays open because the review that must pass is an independent one and every round so far returned FAIL; answering B-1 is not closure and a sixth round decides that.

deviations.summary: The first M3 manifest draft omitted M3-W0 from workPackages even though its gate status appeared elsewhere in the same document. The M3-W8 review treated that as blocking; this revision resolves it by adding M3-W0 to the canonical inventory.

The M3-W8 review found schemas/package.schema.json still required compiled per-target artifacts and could not express the source-only distribution contract ADG-2 selected. Change rkrpplvwpklskyuwvksvmuuyklkwsqlt resolved it as a breaking schema-v1-in-place migration: targets is no longer admitted, source declares a repository and at least one portable file with its SHA-256 digest, and the unsupported-target failure kind was removed with it. The finding is closed and is recorded here so the audit trail keeps it rather than losing it.

This manifest recorded four result digests that bound nothing. Two named content no tracked file had held since a later change edited the record, and the schema could not see it because the schema constrains the shape of a digest and never its value. The cause was that no gate recomputed benchmarks.results[].sha256. verify_evidence_records in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs now hashes every recorded result and fails ravel-verify-scaffold on any mismatch, and it refuses a manifest that records its own digest, which could only ever pass on a value nobody can compute. The same check found the same rot in evidence/m2/manifest.json, whose noop-pipeline.json and pre-world-gate.json digests had gone stale when change rkrpplvwpklskyuwvksvmuuyklkwsqlt edited both records; those are recomputed too. inputs[] is checked at the revision its manifest pins rather than in the working copy, because it names files outside the evidence directory that keep changing after a milestone closes; hashing those in the working copy would rewrite the claim instead of verifying it. A second M3-W8 review round then found the same rot in a third place: evidence/m0/manifest.json records four more digests under platformEvidence[].baselines[], two of which name tracked evidence records, and nothing recomputed those either. Those two are now bound the same way as benchmarks.results[] and are named by path so the check can find them. The remaining two name private launch validations held outside the repository, which no gate can hash; the check announces them as unbound rather than passing over them in silence.

The revision block pins two different things and the schema says so: changeId is the change that holds this manifest, which the milestone gate recomputes against the change that introduced the file and which therefore stays xqmmlnzmtkqpuuxymttpzqyvnovxtxtv for as long as the file lives, while id is the commit the recorded commands ran on. That id had gone stale by several described changes, so the commands and tests blocks attested to a tree that no longer existed. They were re-run rather than re-pinned from memory, and id now names the commit the run was made on. That is circular to the extent that recording a result changes the tree that produced it: the gate was run to completion over this content, its numbers written here, and then run again over the file as it now stands, with the second run reported in the change description rather than recursively rewritten into these fields. It is the same convention evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json uses for its own gate digests. The inputs digests were recomputed by hand in the same pass, because a manifest that pins one revision and hashes its inputs at another is the defect in a second costume. lineCoveragePercent now takes the Lines column of cargo llvm-cov, which is what the field name says; an earlier draft took the region column, which is why the figure moved down while coverage went up. The block was re-run and re-pinned again for the same reason when docs/architecture/m3-hook-targets.md was corrected: an input digest is hashed at revision.id, so correcting a pinned input means the recorded run moves with it. durationMs is measured rather than remembered, and a fifth-round follow-up was right that the previous value was bound by nothing: it is now the wall clock of the run this block records, taken around the whole devenv tasks run ravel:verify invocation. It is a warm-cache figure and should be read as one — the cargo target directory, the JVM harness artifacts and the coverage instrumentation were all already built, so a cold run on the same machine costs several minutes and this number is not a claim about one. Nothing binds it: the log it belongs to is private, which is the same ceiling verify_recorded_run already records for the counts beside it.

This manifest and the records it inventories disagreed on whether Ravel had moved its own versioned bytes through a world save and reload. The manifest said it had not; evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json and evidence/m3/README.md said it had. The records were right and the manifest was stale: change uyvzkzzstmrsunzxznznwqorvxslnklr put a world-owning mod in the production composition and the round trip was observed after it. Every tracked record now says the same thing, with the same ceiling attached. Relatedly, linux-process-matrix.json recorded result pass for M3-W7 while this manifest held M3-W7 open; the record was right and this manifest now closes the gate.

The review.record.sha256 field meant three different things across the four manifests and no gate could tell them apart. evidence/m0/manifest.json recorded b225d06b3f4b, which is exactly sha256 of evidence/m0/review.md, a tracked file that nothing recomputed; evidence/m1/manifest.json and evidence/m2/manifest.json recorded digests that match no tracked file, which was read at the time as those records being deliberately private and turned out to mean the digests bound nothing obtainable; this manifest recorded no review record at all. The rule now exists: schemas/evidence.schema.json requires review.record.name to be a repository-relative path inside the milestone directory, and verify_recorded_review in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs recomputes its digest through the same verify_tracked_digest body as results and baselines, so the scaffold fails on a review record that names prose or hashes the wrong bytes. M0's record is renamed to review.md against its unchanged digest, M1's and this milestone's name tracked verdicts written for the purpose, and M2's is withdrawn because the review it stood for was never written into the repository. Renaming a title to a path is not what closed this; recomputing the digest is.

verify_evidence_records has no floor. It discovers manifests by scanning the evidence directory, so an unreadable, renamed, or absent evidence/ yields zero manifests, zero violations, and no message, and a digest check that verifies nothing is indistinguishable from one that verified everything. Every other hole in this machinery announces itself; this one is the failure mode the check cannot report on itself. A floor means naming the milestones that must be present, which is a decision about what the scaffold contract owns rather than a repair to the digest check, so it is recorded here instead.

The third M3-W8 review found that verify_recorded_change and verify_manifest_change returned silently on a checkout with no .jj repository, so on a git-only clone the control their own doc comment calls the repository's strongest provenance control evaporated without a word — unlike verify_recorded_inputs, which announces the same skip. Both now announce it. The same change added verify_recorded_run, which holds every milestone manifest's recorded gate run to its own arithmetic on every ravel-verify-scaffold rather than only at the milestone the gate is closing: counts that sum to the total, no failures, no skips, coverage at or above the floor, and no manifest recording a gate run without a test result. What no check can bind is the run itself: the log is private and the pinned revision is below the tip by construction.

This manifest's revision, commands, and tests blocks describe the revision revision.id pins and not the state they sit in, and evidence/m3/README.md said otherwise until it was corrected. revision.id 3c3520be is an ancestor of the tip, below every change that landed after it; the fourth review round found the earlier wording here counting those changes, which was true when it was written and false one commit later, so this record states the relationship and leaves the count to jj log. tests.total is that revision's 813, which is not the count the tip runs and cannot be, because every change above it that adds a test moves the tip's; commands[0].logSha256 and the M3-W7 verificationLogSha256 name that run's log. That is not drift but arithmetic: recording a gate result changes the tree that produced it, so revision.id can never be the tip commit and no manifest can claim the identity the README claimed for it. The convention is the one evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json uses for its own gate digests — run the gate over the content, write the numbers, then run both gates again over the file as it stands and report the second run in the change description. What is bound rather than trusted is that revision.id resolves, because verify_recorded_inputs hashes every input there, and that the recorded numbers agree with each other, because verify_recorded_run checks them on every scaffold run.

Two passages in evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json were reconciled rather than left contradicting each other. worldPersistenceRoundTrip.worldRemovedAfterwards.whatSurvivesTheRemoval read as though a digest restored checkability once the world was gone, while reviewCeiling in the same object says that a digest of a vanished file records a claim rather than verifies one; the passage now keeps the ceiling's position, and evidence/m3/README.md no longer echoes the old wording. rewrite.worldOnlyTargets listed eight targets with no stated membership rule, so worldOnlyTargetsCriterion now gives it: a target is listed when opening a world is what puts it on the path, which is narrower than being unreachable at the title screen, and server.tick, server.tick-integrated, save.save-everything, and save.set-dirty are named as the targets that difference excludes. The 15 − 4 = 11 and 33 − 6 = 27 arithmetic is unaffected, being per class and per rewritten method.

The earliest M3-W8 round's verdict text is untracked and not recoverable. The four blocking findings this manifest and evidence/m3/README.md attribute to it survive as prose summary only: evidence/m3/review.md has never held that round, no other tracked file has ever held a review record for M3, and change xqmmlnzmtkqpuuxymttpzqyvnovxtxtv, which recorded the round's outcome, touched only the README and this manifest. So there is no clause table, no anchor, no statement of what that reviewer recomputed or could not reach, and no way to check the summary against what was written — including whether four is the number of findings raised. The fourth round found this, and it is answered by stating it in review.md and counting the round in every count here rather than by reconstructing a verdict nobody has.

The fourth M3-W8 round found evidence/m3/profiling-overhead.json publishing two derived figures a reader could not follow: overhead.perTick.formula applied to the two-decimal percentiles printed beside it yields 500.05 where nanoseconds records 510.05, and breakEven.crossingsPerTick reconciles only against the unrounded per-crossing percentile of 0.051. The figures were right and the derivation was unstateable. The record now carries overhead.rounding, which says that every figure is rounded to two decimals while the derived pair is computed from the unrounded percentiles. Nothing writes that field for the record — the measurement writes the numbers, not the prose about them — so the_record_states_the_rounding_the_derived_figures_were_computed_under in tests/conformance/tests/profiling_report.rs is what stops a re-run or an edit from dropping it, rather than the measurement. A fifth-round follow-up found the accompanying passage in evidence/m3/README.md wrong in the opposite direction: it said the tick-boundary percentile was recoverable only as far as the interval that rounds to 0.05 and that neither derived figure moved inside it, when breakEven divides by 0.051 and therefore moves about 19.6 per nanosecond of boundary time. The published 9803920.59 pins the unrounded boundary to roughly [0.0497, 0.0502], about twenty times narrower than the rounding interval, and perTick is the figure that recovers it no better than the rounding. The README now states that, with both intervals derived rather than asserted.

The fourth M3-W8 round found change_mismatch in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs treating empty output from introducing_change as agreement, so any path jj could not attribute cleared the repository's strongest provenance control in silence — the same failure mode the third round raised one level up, where the .jj skips were. It now announces that it cleared without a verdict, the way those skips do. What remains carried rather than fixed is that a cleared control is still a control that did not run, which no message changes.

M3-W8 found no hook-integrity defect in the inventory itself: minecraft/versions/26.1.2/hooks.toml, the generated mappings.lock, the transformed-class counts and the callable-target counts reconcile. That was three of the four things this row used to claim. The fourth, docs/architecture/m3-hook-targets.md, did not: it still said 35 entries, 31 methods and 23 handle parameters after ADG-7's two world persistence seams brought the inventory to 37 entries, 33 methods and 27 handle parameters, while tabling those two seams further down the same file. This manifest closes M3-W0 on that document and pins its digest under inputs[], and a digest binds bytes rather than the thing the bytes are about, so the gate was satisfied by a stale document and nothing in the repository referenced it from any .rs, .sh or .nix. The counts are corrected and verify_hook_inventory_document in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs now derives all four from hooks.toml on every ravel-verify-scaffold and fails when the document disagrees, checking every occurrence rather than the first. The inventory itself is untouched, so no re-pin ceremony was owed.

All three M3 measurement trials were run on a dirty working copy and no revision identifies the code they measured. evidence/m3/pack-compile.json records trial.revision.dirty true at both its curve trial and its variants trial, and evidence/m3/profiling-overhead.json records it at its own, so in each case the recorded changeId and id name a commit the measured tree differed from by an unrecorded amount. That reaches the one limit ravel:verify enforces on every run: the M3-W6 budget in profiling-overhead.json is compared against a later measurement by cargo xtask verify budget, and the code behind the figure it compares against is not identified. It is disclosed rather than repaired. Re-measuring clean is not cheap — the curve trial ran 174 s, the variants trial 1161 s, and both hold only on the linux-reference-v1 hardware profile, so a re-run on any other machine remeasures rather than reproduces — and a re-measurement would land on a working copy that is dirty again for the same structural reason the manifest's own revision block records: recording a result changes the tree that produced it. What is bound rather than trusted is the limit and the arithmetic over it, which tests/conformance/tests/profiling_report.rs and cargo xtask verify budget check on every gate; what is not bound is which source produced the measurement. Note that verify_general_closure requires this manifest's own revision.dirty to be false, so the milestone gate holds the manifest to a standard the trials it inventories do not meet. That disclosure was prose alone and bound nothing: the pins it describes are now listed under unobtainableRevisions above, each quoting the record, commit and change it excuses. verify_admitted_revisions in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs now applies the same visible-commit and changeId-owns-id tests to every pin inside every record a manifest admits, on every ravel:verify rather than in an opt-in task, and permits a failing pin only where unobtainableRevisions above quotes that record, that commit and that change. So the inventory is that list rather than a number in this sentence, a pin nothing discloses fails the gate, and a disclosure the defect has outlived fails it too.

ADG-7's save-seam refusal had no test until this pass. docs/decisions/adg-7-world-persistence.md and jvm/bootstrap/dev/ravel/jvm/Persistence.java specify that an absent installed-prologue marker for worldSavePersistence refuses the world load, and saveSeamInstalled returned true in all eight cases the JVM harness ran, so the false branch of the one check that distinguishes a transformed class from a present one never executed anywhere in the gate. jvm/harness/run-harness.sh now runs a ninth world lifecycle, missing-save-seam, which installs the open seam and not the save seam: the server class is present and loads, its transformation matches no method, the marker stays empty, and the world is refused with the recorded diagnostic before Rust is asked at all. The stand-in inventory selects that arrangement from ravel.test.persistence.saveSeamMissing rather than from a broken descriptor, so the case exercises the marker and nothing else.
M3-W8 found no safety, layering, or ADR-conformance defect in the reviewed prototype stack.
M3-W8 found no redaction defect in the tracked evidence; raw launcher, account, world, and capture material remains outside the repository.

Nothing requires a milestone manifest to list the records that sit beside it, so a record can be added to a milestone directory and be digest-bound by nothing. evidence/m0/manifest.json is the live case: benchmarks.results is empty while two evidence records sit in that directory. Those two are now bound through platformEvidence[].baselines[].result instead, but only because the baselines happen to name them; a third record added tomorrow would be bound by neither. The gate recomputes what a manifest claims and never asks whether the claims cover the directory.

This manifest records platformEvidence as an empty array even though M3-W7 is an operator-run native Linux matrix, so the general closure rule over platformEvidence[].commands[].exitStatus contributes nothing for M3 and the matrix is bound only through the benchmarks.results digest of evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json. Whether an operator-run matrix belongs in platformEvidence, and what a platform record would mean for a campaign whose raw material is deliberately outside the repository, is a judgement left open rather than answered here.

revision.id is re-pinned to 724f12b6b80c3f0597c5b7bf4a40b1fdc41e2315, the commit change xqmmlnzmtkqpuuxymttpzqyvnovxtxtv is at now, and every input digest is re-hashed there. It named 584abc1bc1da00910b90655042befd907ea8733d before, a commit jj abandoned when it rewrote that change. That commit still resolved in this working copy, out of its operation log, and resolved nowhere else, so a cold reviewer's fresh clone found every input digest recorded here unreadable and the scaffold gate refused the clone. verify_pinned_commit in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs now requires revision.id to be a commit visible history reaches and to be the commit its own changeId is at, on every ravel:verify rather than only in the opt-in milestone task, so the next rewrite of this change fails the gate and forces a re-pin instead of dangling in silence. Re-pinning does not repair the run. commands[] and tests were recorded against 584abc1bc1da00910b90655042befd907ea8733d, so revision.id no longer names the tree they were measured on, and nothing recomputes them: tests.total and tests.lineCoveragePercent are held only to their own arithmetic and to the coverage floor, and no tracked artifact binds either figure to a gate run. They are read here as an attestation that M3's gate was run and passed at that revision, not as evidence a reader can re-derive. Binding a redacted gate summary instead was available and refused: the summary would have to come from a re-run on today's tree, whose numbers are not the ones recorded, so it would bind a different run than the one attested. What revision.id does bind is the input digests, and the gate recomputes all of them there on every run.

The recompute a reader gets outside this working copy is bounded, and both bounds were measured rather than assumed. A git clone --no-local of this repository carries no refs/jj/* at all: in that clone 584abc1bc1da00910b90655042befd907ea8733d, the commit this manifest pinned before the re-pin, does not exist as an object, while 724f12b6b80c3f0597c5b7bf4a40b1fdc41e2315 is visible and every input digest recorded here recomputes there. So the reachability half is repaired, and it is repaired because the colocated repository exports the visible stack to git HEAD, which a clone follows. What a clone does not get is a jj repository, and without one verify_recorded_inputs and verify_manifest_change announce on stdout that they are skipping rather than reporting a pass; the reader has to run jj git init --colocate before the provenance block means anything. What remains beyond that is publication: nothing in this stack has been pushed, so these commits live in this repository and in clones taken directly from it, and a reader working from a remote has whatever that remote carries and no more. That is disclosed rather than closed because pushing is not in this work's scope, and no claim is made that publishing is imminent. It is classified non-blocking because the provenance checks fail closed — an unresolvable or moved revision is a violation, never a silent pass — and because publishing the stack changes no evidence in this manifest.

risks.summary: M3-W4 and M3-W7 close on evidence a reviewer cannot recompute. The world round trip was observed in a real client, but the world, the raw logs, and the screenshots were deleted when the campaign finished and only their digests were kept. A digest of a file that no longer exists records a claim rather than verifies one, so the live half of both gates is operator attestation. What is independently checkable is the in-gate half: tests/conformance/tests/saved_data.rs and jvm/harness/PersistenceMain.java run under ravel:verify on any machine. This is the repository's established convention for launch evidence rather than a departure from it, and it is stated here so that no reader mistakes an attested result for a recomputable one.

The absent-aggregate case ADG-7 initializes fresh state for has in-gate proof and no live proof. It was observed once, on a world that held no data/ravel directory, and the same campaign then wrote an aggregate into that world, so the observation is not re-checkable on this instance. a_world_holding_no_data_this_mod_owns_initializes_fresh_state in tests/conformance/tests/saved_data.rs is what still proves it. Proving it live again would need a world never opened with Ravel attached.

Two profiling counters have never been observed above zero in a real client. tick-count cannot leave zero at all, because nothing on the game's tick path marks a tick boundary at M3; the screen names it unmeasurable rather than stating a figure. The command counter is different: its increment path exists in the production graph and the conformance suite exercises it, and it read zero for the honest reason that the commands typed were vanilla and unnamespaced and neither mod in the composed host claims a command. Demonstrating it live is a composition change, not a collector change.

M3 is not closed. Six independent M3-W8 rounds have run and all six returned FAIL. Five of the six verdicts are tracked verbatim at evidence/m3/review.md and bound by review.record; the earliest round's verdict text was never written into the repository and is not recoverable from it, so that round survives only as the summary in this manifest's M3-W8 row and in evidence/m3/README.md, and review.md says so rather than counting itself complete. The fifth tracked round's blocking finding B-1 is answered: profilingReObservationCampaign in evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json re-observed the profiling report at both GUI scales against a screen jar and native library hashed before the launch, so the M3-W7 profiling row is no longer bound to a build that could not have produced it, and the earlier unattributable reading is withdrawn rather than reworded. Answering it changes nothing about closure. One of that round's must-fix findings and all five moderate and six minor findings are still unanswered, no round has yet returned a pass, and the review that must pass is an independent one, so M3-W8 is what remains and until it closes M3 authorizes no private inventory work.

M3-W0 is as unrecomputable as the live half of M3-W4 and M3-W7, and until now no M3 record said so. That gate closes on docs/architecture/m3-hook-targets.md and the pinned 26.1.2 hook inventory, both tracked, which reads as recomputable evidence — but every claim either file makes about the game is a claim about the pinned client jar, and that jar is a restricted local fixture this repository never tracks. On a machine without it the chain terminates at minecraft/versions/26.1.2/adapter.toml's inputs.clientJar sha256 and bytes: mappings.lock and stubs.lock can be compared against their own pinned hashes, which is what catches a stale lock and is stated in adapter.toml's own comments, but no member can be re-resolved against a class file and no count in the inventory can be re-derived from the game. What a reviewer can recompute is the inventory's internal consistency — which verify_hook_inventory_document now includes the document in — and nothing beyond it. evidence/m3/README.md states the same ceiling in the same terms.

One excluded diagnostic launch and the first W7 launch remained alive after the normal game shutdown sequence. The accepted W7 relaunch exited naturally, so the recurring post-shutdown futex hang is tracked separately and does not invalidate the matrix's supporting evidence.

The exact-version package refusal M3-W4's gate names cannot be reached from a launch. SavedDataAggregate::open compares an envelope's requiredPackages against an installed set, and crates/ravel-bootstrap/src/persistence.rs has no such set to give it: install() receives a lifecycle machine, a mod set and a pre-world report, LifecycleEntry and HostMod carry an identity and no version, and ravel-composed-host builds its mods from source rather than from package manifests. So a stored requirement refuses as missing, which is fail-closed and is what SPEC.md §14 asks for, while SavedDataError::IncompatiblePackage — required and installed at different versions — is unreachable in the game process. It is reachable and asserted where an installed set exists: ravel-save's own suite and tests/conformance/tests/saved_data.rs, which supply one. The gap is that no launch supplies one, and closing it means carrying package identity and version through composition into install(), which belongs to the packaged-installation work M4-W5 owns rather than to a source-composed prototype. The seam says so in code at the call site, and no branch is left in persistence.rs looking like a check that runs.
